title: Hidden in Plain Sight: The Role of Corporate Board of Directors in Public Charity Lobbying
eligible_reason: Every reported regression includes time-varying lagged controls (local controls = csize_lag1 size_lag1 roa_lag1 q_lag1 lev_lag1), which the protocol excludes. The main regressor contd_lag1 (lagged firm-charity board connection) switches on and off rather than being an absorbing adoption indicator. The DiD around exogenous director departures (Table 6, treatxpost) is run on propensity-score-matched cohorts (kmatch) with the same controls, and the event study (Figure 2) also carries controls. The package contains SAS/Stata code and logs only; the raw inputs (BoardEx, Compustat, IRS 990, LDA reports via WRDS/AWS/SOPR) are not shipped.
design_notes: Firm-charity-year panel (final_sample, not shipped), FE indiv_gid (firm x charity pair) + time_gid (tax year) or firm + charity + year, cluster indiv_gid. Table 3: log_ccl_new / ccl_new_scaled (connected-charity lobbying) on contd_lag1 + controls. Tables 4, 5, 7, 8: variants, bill-level alignment, cross-sectional splits. Table 6 A/B: treatxpost on PSM-matched turnover cohorts (exo turnover = retirement/age 65/death); Table 6C similar. Figure 2: base treatxpre3..treatxpost3 event study with controls. Table 10: nypost (New York transparency law) on charity panel, cluster state. Table 11: contributions.
n_adoption_cohorts_note: Connections form and dissolve in many years (staggered in principle), but the treatment is not absorbing and no data are shipped to count cohorts.
data_access_note: No analysis data in package; README lists WRDS (Compustat, CRSP, BoardEx, 13F, Insider), Refinitiv ESG, Trucost, Maplight, IRS 990 (AWS), LDA reports (SOPR), USASpending, FEC as required inputs. Only code + log files shipped.
screener_notes: Not a staggered-adoption design in the Hull sense: connection indicator is a switching regressor with lagged controls in every column. Even the turnover DiD (Table 6) relies on PSM matching plus controls.
